Datasheet sections this page relies on Instruction packet layout: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 2 Instruction Packet, p. 1 Status packet, error byte and alert bit: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 3 Status Packet; 3.2 Error, p. 1 Response policy and the broadcast ID: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 3.4 Response Policy, p. 1 Packet process, header and byte stuffing: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 4 Packet Process, p. 1 Ping, Read, Write, Reg Write, Action: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 5.1 Ping to 5.5 Action, p. 1 Factory Reset, Reboot, Clear, Control Table Backup: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 5.6 Factory Reset to 5.9 Control Table Backup, p. 1 Sync Read, Sync Write, Fast Sync Read: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 5.10 Sync Read; 5.11 Sync Write; 5.12 Fast Sync Read, p. 1 Bulk Read, Bulk Write, Fast Bulk Read: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 5.13 Bulk Read; 5.14 Bulk Write; 5.15 Fast Bulk Read, p. 1 Protocol 1.0 packets and checksum: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 1.0 web page, no revision mark, 2 Instruction Packet; 2.6 Checksum; 3 Status Packet; 3.2 Checksum, p. 1 Protocol 1.0 instructions: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 1.0 web page, no revision mark, 4 Instruction Details (Ping to Bulk Read), p. 1 Protocol 1.0 error byte: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 1.0 web page, no revision mark, 3.1 Error, p. 1 CRC-16 of protocol 2.0 packets: ROBOTIS e-Manual, CRC Calculation web page, no revision mark, CRC Calculation, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . One bus, one protocol ¶ Every servo on a bus speaks the same protocol, chosen by Config::protocol . Protocol 2.0 is the one of the X series, the MX(2.0) servos and the XL-320; protocol 1.0 is the one of the AX, RX, DX and MX (1.0 firmware) servos. The X330, XL430, XM, XH, XD and XW servos can be set to either (their Protocol Type register). The driver does not detect the protocol: a wrong choice shows as Error::Timeout on every call, because a servo drops a packet it cannot parse. Protocol 2.0 packets ¶ Field Bytes Value Header 4 FF FF FD 00 ID 1 0 to 252; 254 is the broadcast ID Length 2 The bytes after this field: instruction, parameters, CRC Instruction 1 See the table below; 55 in a status packet Parameters n Stuffed CRC 2 CRC-16, polynomial 0x8005 , initial value 0, low byte first, over everything before it A status packet carries the error byte and then the parameters. Bit 7 of the error byte is the alert (the servo has a hardware error pending, see its Hardware Error Status register); bits 6 to 0 are the error number ( Protocol2Error ). Byte stuffing. The header must not occur inside a packet, so the sender inserts one FD after every FF FF FD in the parameters, and the Length counts the inserted byte. protocol::FrameWriter stuffs while it builds a packet and protocol::Destuff() removes it from a reply; an FF FF FD not followed by FD is a bad packet ( Error::InvalidReply ). The driver sizes its buffer for the worst case: every third parameter byte stuffed. Protocol 1.0 packets ¶ Field Bytes Value Header 2 FF FF ID 1 0 to 253; 254 is the broadcast ID Length 1 Parameters plus 2 Instruction 1 In a status packet, the error byte Parameters n 0 to 253 Checksum 1 The complement of the low byte of the sum from the ID to the last parameter The error byte is a set of flags ( p1_error ). The driver splits them in two: the command faults (angle limit, range, checksum, instruction) mean the servo did not carry out the instruction and give Error::DeviceError ; the conditions (input voltage, overheating, overload) report the servo's state next to valid data and are handled by Config::alert_policy . Instructions ¶ Instruction Code Protocol Driver call Ping 01 1.0, 2.0 Ping() , Identify() , BroadcastPing() , ScanIds() Read 02 1.0, 2.0 Read() , ReadRegister() , ReadFeedback() Write 03 1.0, 2.0 Write() , WriteRegister() , SetTorque() , SetGoalPosition() Reg Write 04 1.0, 2.0 RegWrite() Action 05 1.0, 2.0 Action() Factory Reset 06 1.0, 2.0 FactoryReset() Reboot 08 1.0, 2.0 Reboot() Clear 10 2.0 Clear() Control Table Backup 20 2.0 Backup() Sync Read 82 2.0 SyncRead() Sync Write 83 1.0, 2.0 SyncWrite() Fast Sync Read 8A 2.0 FastSyncRead() Bulk Read 92 1.0 (MX and X servos), 2.0 BulkRead() Bulk Write 93 2.0 BulkWrite() Fast Bulk Read 9A 2.0 FastBulkRead() A call for an instruction the configured protocol does not have returns Error::Unsupported before anything is sent. Who answers ¶ A servo answers according to its Status Return Level register ( StatusReturn ): a ping always, a read at level 1 and 2, every other instruction at level 2 only. Config::status_return is what the driver expects of the whole bus; a call that needs an answer the level does not give returns Unsupported instead of waiting for a timeout. The broadcast ID is answered only for a ping, a sync read and a bulk read (and by each servo in turn: the answers come in ID order, one reply timeout apart for a broadcast ping, Config::broadcast_timeout_us ). A write or an action on the broadcast ID is sent and Ok means "sent". Finding the reply ¶ The receive bytes can hold garbage, the echo of the request, or a late reply. protocol::Scan() looks for the first valid status packet: It skips bytes until a header. A partial header at the end is kept, because the next read may complete it. A candidate needs a plausible length (it must fit the receive buffer) and, in protocol 2.0, the status instruction 55 . A candidate whose CRC or checksum does not match is dropped by one byte, and the search goes on inside it, so a real packet that starts within damaged bytes is still found. Each such drop is counted in Stats::crc_errors . A packet shorter than its length says is waited for, bounded by Config::gap_timeout_us per read. A line that carries only 00 or only FF for a whole candidate is a stuck or floating line: Error::LineFault (counted in Stats::line_faults ), not a timeout, so the wiring is blamed and not the servo. Fast Sync Read and Fast Bulk Read ¶ The servos answer back to back inside one status packet: the first one sends the header, its own part and a CRC, and each following servo continues the same packet with its part (error byte, ID, data, CRC). The driver parses the parts one by one, checks each CRC, and fills DeviceReply per ID. A packet that ends early still delivers the parts that arrived whole and checked; the rest are Timeout . The e-Manual gives the layout of the parts, not what the first servo puts in the packet header's ID field or the length when a listed servo is silent; the driver accepts the header of any ID and re-reads the parts it can verify (see Troubleshooting and the open points in the Contract ). Use the plain SyncRead() where the servos' firmware does not list Fast Sync Read ( SupportsFastRead() is advice built from the e-Manual's firmware notes).

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then move a servo from your MCU: wire the bus, write a small port class, call four driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on Byte to byte time and the packet gap: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 1.6 Byte to Byte Time, p. 1 Control table, X series (addresses, sizes, units): ROBOTIS e-Manual, XM430-W350 web page, no revision mark, 2 Control Table; 2.1 Control Table of EEPROM Area; 2.2 Control Table of RAM Area, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated bus of two XM430 servos, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/dynamixel_host_example DYNAMIXEL driver 0.1.0 on the host dynamixel: initialised servo 1: model 1020, firmware 46 servo 2: model 1020, firmware 46 servo 1: 31 C servo 2: 25 C torque off The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU Servo bus Notes UART TX and RX DATA, through a half-duplex stage 57 600 8N1 for an X-series servo at the factory settings A GPIO or the UART's RTS The stage's direction input High while the MCU sends GND GND Common with the servo supply VDD 10.0 V to 14.8 V from its own supply (XM430-W350), never from the MCU board The Hardware page has the pins, the circuit, the bus settings and the timing. Check the servo's ID, bit rate and protocol first (the Dynamixel Wizard of ROBOTIS shows them); the driver defaults are protocol 2.0, 57 600 bit/s and ID 1. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the dynamixel::dynamixel CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-dynamixel.git external/driver-dynamixel 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the UART up and moves bytes. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public dynamixel :: UartInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the UART up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } // Transmit the whole packet in one go, wait for the last stop bit, then listen again. bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_send ( data , len ); } // One to `max` bytes as soon as one has arrived, or 0 after `timeout_us` without a byte. std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_us ) noexcept { return platform_uart_receive ( data , max , timeout_us ); } // Drop whatever has been received and not yet read. bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_discard_input (); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds (the settle times after a reboot or a baud rate change). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the half-duplex rules. 4. Move the servo ¶ main.cpp #include "dynamixel.hpp" int move_first_servo ( MyPort & port ) { dynamixel :: DYNAMIXEL < MyPort > servos ( port ); // protocol 2.0, 57 600 bit/s; no I/O yet if ( auto r = servos . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. UART up return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus: check the UART and the wiring } const auto found = servos . Ping ( 1 ); // 2. who is there? model, firmware, family if ( ! found ) { return static_cast < int > ( found . error ); // Timeout: wrong ID, baud rate or protocol } const dynamixel :: ServoRef servo { found . value . id , found . value . family }; if ( auto r = servos . SetTorque ( servo , true ); ! r ) { // 3. torque on return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } return static_cast < int > ( servos . SetGoalPosition ( servo , 2048 ). error ); // 4. half a turn } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() brings the UART up through your port and applies Config::baud . It sends nothing on the bus. Ping(1) asks servo 1 for its model number and firmware. The model number selects the control table ( PingInfo::family ) that the typed calls below use. SetTorque() writes the Torque Enable register of the servo's family. SetGoalPosition() writes the Goal Position register. The torque must be on first; position 2048 is the middle of the 4096 counts of an X-series servo. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() : the UART did not come up Ping() returns Timeout The servo's supply, its ID, bit rate and protocol; the direction pin Ping() returns LineFault The line is stuck low, high or floating: power, ground, the half-duplex stage Ping() returns EchoMismatch Single-wire loopback is on and the echo differs: another talker, or Config::echo is wrong A call returns DeviceError The servo refused the instruction; GetLastReply().error_byte says why Troubleshooting goes through each. Examples : the host example and the ESP32 example. Platforms : which MCUs have a port and an example.

docs.title: 2. Add the driver

docs.text: The port is the only platform code: it brings the UART up and moves bytes. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public dynamixel :: UartInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the UART up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } // Transmit the whole packet in one go, wait for the last stop bit, then listen again. bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_send ( data , len ); } // One to `max` bytes as soon as one has arrived, or 0 after `timeout_us` without a byte. std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t max , uint32_t timeout_us ) noexcept { return platform_uart_receive ( data , max , timeout_us ); } // Drop whatever has been received and not yet read. bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_discard_input (); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds (the settle times after a reboot or a baud rate change). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the half-duplex rules.
docs.title: 3. Write the port

docs.text: main.cpp #include "dynamixel.hpp" int move_first_servo ( MyPort & port ) { dynamixel :: DYNAMIXEL < MyPort > servos ( port ); // protocol 2.0, 57 600 bit/s; no I/O yet if ( auto r = servos . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. UART up return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus: check the UART and the wiring } const auto found = servos . Ping ( 1 ); // 2. who is there? model, firmware, family if ( ! found ) { return static_cast < int > ( found . error ); // Timeout: wrong ID, baud rate or protocol } const dynamixel :: ServoRef servo { found . value . id , found . value . family }; if ( auto r = servos . SetTorque ( servo , true ); ! r ) { // 3. torque on return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } return static_cast < int > ( servos . SetGoalPosition ( servo , 2048 ). error ); // 4. half a turn } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() brings the UART up through your port and applies Config::baud . It sends nothing on the bus. Ping(1) asks servo 1 for its model number and firmware. The model number selects the control table ( PingInfo::family ) that the typed calls below use. SetTorque() writes the Torque Enable register of the servo's family. SetGoalPosition() writes the Goal Position register. The torque must be on first; position 2048 is the middle of the 4096 counts of an X-series servo. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers.

docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver. an unseen device reset ¶ Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?" RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read ¶ Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?" RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data ¶ Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?" RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something ¶ Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?" RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused ¶ Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends." RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack ¶ Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?" RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading ¶ Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?" RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard ¶ Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?" RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard ¶ Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?" RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read ¶ Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b. Datasheet and documentation classes ¶ RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing ¶ Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?" RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit ¶ Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?" RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks ¶ Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return. RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim ¶ Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample. RD-32 Docs style ¶ Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09. RD-33 Another project's name or dated history ¶ Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py . Process and test-quality classes ¶ RD-25 Guards no test kills ¶ Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes. RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules ¶ Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?" RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule ¶ Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit. RD-19 Template drift ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate. RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI ¶ Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count). CI-only checks (MISRA scan, ESP-IDF, compile-fail) ¶ RD-11 Header outside the library subset ¶ Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep). RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic ¶ Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != . RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses ¶ Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests . RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain ¶ Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned). RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended. RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp . RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type ¶ Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?" RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 ¶ Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision. RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete ¶ Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call. RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults ¶ Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?" RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler ¶ Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert . RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA ¶ Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.text: The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.

docs.title: Index

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"
docs.title: RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"
docs.title: RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read

docs.text: Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
docs.title: RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data

docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"
docs.title: RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b.
docs.title: RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read

docs.text: Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?"
docs.title: RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing

docs.text: Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?"
docs.title: RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit

docs.text: Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return.
docs.title: RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks

docs.text: Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample.
docs.title: RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim

docs.text: Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09.
docs.title: RD-32 Docs style

docs.text: Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py .
docs.title: RD-33 Another project's name or dated history

docs.text: Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).
docs.title: RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI

docs.text: Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep).
docs.title: RD-11 Header outside the library subset

docs.text: Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != .
docs.title: RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic

docs.text: Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests .
docs.title: RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses

docs.text: Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned).
docs.title: RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended.
docs.title: RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp .
docs.title: RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ

docs.text: Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?"
docs.title: RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type

docs.text: Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision.
docs.title: RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2

docs.text: Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call.
docs.title: RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete

docs.text: Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?"
docs.title: RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults

docs.text: Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert .
docs.title: RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler

docs.text: Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( dynamixel_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/dynamixel.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target dynamixel_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ Nothing here has been run against a servo. The ESP32 example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it finds the servos on the bus and logs the feedback of each twice a second with the torque off. On the first run, check the four open points of the Contract (a Fast Sync Read of two or more servos, a write of the ID register, a Sync Read with one servo unplugged, the reply deadline) and record the board, the servo models, the firmware versions and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ What each error means on a servo bus, what to look at first, and how to read what the driver kept. Datasheet sections this page relies on Status packet, error byte and alert bit: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 2.0 web page, no revision mark, 3 Status Packet; 3.2 Error, p. 1 Protocol 1.0 error byte: ROBOTIS e-Manual, DYNAMIXEL Protocol 1.0 web page, no revision mark, 3.1 Error, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . First, look at what the driver kept ¶ Every call leaves evidence, with no extra I/O: Call What it tells you GetLastRequest() The bytes of the last instruction packet, as put on the line (stuffed, with CRC) GetLastReply() The decoded error byte of the last status packet: error number, alert flag, protocol GetLatchedAlert() The first hardware alert seen since ClearLatchedAlert() GetStats() Transactions, retries, timeouts, CRC errors, skipped garbage bytes, line faults A growing timeouts with no crc_errors is silence; growing garbage_bytes is noise or a wrong rate; growing crc_errors is damaged packets. Compare GetLastRequest() with what a logic analyser sees: a request that never appears on the wire is the port, one that appears but gets no answer is the servo or the bus. Ping returns Timeout ¶ Nothing answered, or the answer was not a packet the driver could read. In order of likelihood: Cause Check The servo has no power The servo supply: 10.0 V to 14.8 V for the XM430-W350 Wrong ID Ping by ID with ScanIds() (protocol 1.0) or BroadcastPing() (protocol 2.0) Wrong bit rate The servo's Baud Rate register against Config::baud ; X series ship at 57 600, AX at 1 000 000 Wrong protocol Servos of the X330, XL430, XM, XH and XD series can be set to either protocol; AX, RX, DX and MX 1.0 speak 1.0 The line is not turned round The direction pin or half-duplex mode: the reply must be heard ( Hardware ) A reply deadline that is too short Raise Config::reply_timeout_us ( Configuration ); a USB adapter needs UsbAdapterPreset() TX and RX swapped Cross them (a separate-line transceiver), or check the single-wire stage Calls return LineFault ¶ The line carried only 00 or only FF for a whole candidate packet, or did not go quiet within 16 flush rounds. The wiring is at fault, not the servo: the data line is stuck low (a short, a servo with no power pulling it down, the transmitter left enabled), stuck high or floating (no pull-up, the transmitter disabled and nothing driving it). Check the direction control and the pull-up, then call Resync() . Calls return EchoMismatch ¶ Config::echo is Loopback and the bytes read back are not the bytes sent: another device is talking at the same time (two masters, a servo that answers a broadcast it should not), or the wiring does not loop back. If TX and RX are not tied, set EchoMode::None . Calls return Crc, or garbage_bytes grows ¶ Packets arrive damaged. Check, in this order: the bit rate (a rate error of more than 2 to 3 percent damages bytes), the ground between the master and the servos, the length of the cable and its termination at a high rate, and a port that shifts bytes (a Read() that returns more than it was given, a FIFO that overflows). A single Crc is retried for a read; a write is not repeated, so a Crc on a write means the reply was damaged, not that the instruction failed. Calls return InvalidReply ¶ The bytes looked like a status packet but broke a rule: the length does not fit, the instruction is not a status instruction, the parameter count is wrong for the read, or a protocol 2.0 packet has an unstuffed header. A servo of another protocol on the bus produces this; so does a reply to an older request that arrived late. Call Resync() to empty the line. Calls return DeviceError ¶ The servo understood the packet and refused it. Read GetLastReply() : Protocol 2.0 error number Meaning Typical cause 1 Result Fail The instruction could not be processed Wrong state, a register not allowed now 2 Instruction Error Undefined instruction, or Action without Reg Write A call the servo's firmware does not have 3 CRC Error The servo's CRC check failed A damaged request 4 Data Range Error The value is outside the register's range A goal beyond a limit 5 Data Length Error The data is shorter than the register A write of the wrong size 6 Data Limit Error The value exceeds the register's limit A goal above the servo's limit 7 Access Error Write to a read-only register, or a protected one Writing the EEPROM area while the torque is on The most common one: a write to an EEPROM register (ID, baud rate, limits, operating mode) with the torque on. Turn the torque off first ( SetTorque(servo, false) ). Calls return DeviceFault ¶ The servo reported a hardware alert (bit 7 of the error byte in protocol 2.0) and Config::alert_policy is Fail . Read Reg::HardwareErrorStatus for the cause: input voltage, overheating, motor encoder, electrical shock or overload. With AlertPolicy::Report (the default) the call succeeds and the alert is latched: poll GetLatchedAlert() . Calls return NotPermitted or Unsupported ¶ Error Cause Fix NotPermitted A destructive instruction without Config::allow_destructive Set it for that call on purpose ( API guide ) Unsupported The instruction does not exist in the configured protocol, the family has no such register, the servo does not answer at the configured status_return , or the port has no SetBaudRate() Check Protocol and Control tables InvalidArgument A value does not fit the register, an ID is out of range, or the packet does not fit FrameBytes Check the argument; raise FrameBytes for a very long sync read A sync read returns Ok but a device is not Ok ¶ That is by design: Result says the exchange worked, DeviceReply::result says what happened to each servo. A servo that is Timeout did not answer (wrong ID, no power, or it was shifted out of the packet by an earlier silent one); Crc means its part arrived damaged; DeviceError carries the servo's error byte. A packet that ends early still delivers the parts that arrived whole. After a Reboot or Factory Reset nothing answers ¶ The servo restarts and may come back with another ID or bit rate: a Factory Reset with ResetOption::All returns the ID to 1 and the rate to the factory one. Use ResetOption::KeepIdAndBaud to keep them, and wait Config::reboot_wait_us before the next call (the driver does). The servo does not move ¶ Check Why Torque is on Reg::TorqueEnable is 0 at power-up; SetTorque(servo, true) The operating mode Position control is the factory mode of most families; a velocity or PWM mode ignores a goal position The limits A goal outside the min and max position limits is refused or clamped The supply A servo with a weak supply reboots under load: the voltage in ReadFeedback() sags
